title: Strip Outer Parentheses of Each Group
statement:
You get a string s of balanced parentheses. Split it into its top-level groups: the shortest non-empty balanced pieces that, placed one after another, make up s. For example "(())()(()())" splits into "(())", "()" and "(()())".

Remove the outermost opening and closing parenthesis of every group, and return what is left, joined in the original order.

examples.why: The groups lose their outer pair: "(())" → "()", "()" → "", "(()())" → "()()".
One group only. Just its outermost pair goes, not every pair.
Three groups, each just an outer pair, so nothing is left.

constraints: s contains only '(' and ')' and is balanced
hints: How do you know where one group ends? Track something as you scan left to right.
Keep a depth counter. A group ends exactly when the depth returns to 0.
An opening parenthesis is outermost if the depth was 0 before it; a closing one is outermost if the depth becomes 0 after it. Copy every other character.

explain.intuition: A stack of open parentheses tells you how deep you are, but here only its size matters, so a single counter does the job. The outermost ( of a group is the one seen at depth 0, and the outermost ) is the one that brings the depth back to 0. Everything else belongs inside some group and is kept.
steps: Start with depth = 0 and an empty output.
For (: if depth > 0, append it. Then increase depth.
For ): decrease depth first. If depth > 0, append it.
pitfalls: Checking the depth on the wrong side of the update. The opening check uses the depth before the increment, the closing check the depth after the decrement.
Removing every pair at depth 1 and 2, or stripping only the very first and last characters of the whole string. Each group loses exactly one pair.
Building the result with repeated string concatenation in a language where that is quadratic. Collect characters in a list and join once.

solutions.title: Split into groups, then trim each
solutions.idea: Use a stack of open positions to find where each group starts and ends, then keep the inside of each group.

solutions.title: Depth counter
solutions.idea: Keep every character except an opening one seen at depth 0 and a closing one that returns the depth to 0.

followups: Return the number of top-level groups instead. Can you do it without building any string?
The string may also contain [] and {} pairs. What do you need beyond a counter?
